# Current state — pixelkit

What the project believes right now: live terms, constraints, policies and requirements, and what has been found or assessed. Decisions have their own view, `DECISION-HISTORY.md`.

## Policies

### liminalkit is an explicit-state, software-rendered toolkit; abstractions stay visible and optional

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.policy.explicit-state-toolkit/1` · scope `all` · topic `positioning`

liminalkit is positioned as a lightweight GUI toolkit for applications that need direct control over drawing, interaction and resource use: desktop utilities, operational interfaces, kiosks and embedded Linux displays. Caller-owned state, immediate-mode controls and software rendering, with no browser, no retained widget tree, no widget identity map and no mandatory GPU stack. Every new subsystem must make its ownership, allocations and any state kept between frames visible in its signature; a hidden mechanism that undermines predictability needs a strong, recorded justification. Layout helpers are stateless functions from a rectangle to rectangles; a retained layout hierarchy is not added without an overwhelming reason. The toolkit does not aim at feature parity with egui, Dioxus or Freya, and does not try to become a universal application framework.

## Observations

### Windows reported no touchpad source for a precision touchpad's wheel messages without touchpad registration

`verified` · `@pixelkit.observation.windows-touchpad-source-not-reported/1` · scope `path "crates/liminalkit-native/src/win.rs"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-shell/tests/scroll_traces/**"`

Recorded with scroll_capture behind the liminalkit-native host on the owner's Windows 11 machine: 150 wheel samples in one sitting, 89 from the precision touchpad (120ths between 3 and 145, never a multiple of 120) and 61 whole notches from a mouse wheel. The subclass on the winit window called GetCurrentInputMessageSource for each wheel message and none of the 150 samples was marked as touchpad. The same run did read the system wheel settings (3 lines, 3 characters), so the subclass was attached. This matches Microsoft's documentation that IMDT_TOUCHPAD is reported only once the thread has registered as touchpad-aware. One thing was not separated: the recording cannot tell whether the call answered 'mouse' or never matched its message, though the matching is unit-tested. Either way the hint as built gives nothing on this machine. The value-based classifier needed no hint: it classed all 89 as continuous and all 61 as notches. No recording yet contains horizontal movement or a held modifier.

> **Stale** — `watches "crates/liminalkit-native/src/win.rs"` was matched by `bc937a74`, which touched `crates/liminalkit-native/src/win.rs`. See [REVIEW-REQUIRED.md](REVIEW-REQUIRED.md#windows-reported-no-touchpad-source-for-a-precision-touchpads-wheel-messages-without-touchpad-registration).

### What a coarse wheel, a finely graded wheel and a precision touchpad send through winit on Windows

`verified` · `@pixelkit.observation.windows-wheel-and-touchpad-streams/1` · scope `path "crates/liminalkit-shell/src/scroll/**"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-shell/tests/scroll_traces/**"`

Recorded on the owner's Windows 11 machine with scroll_capture (winit 0.30.13, host delivery timestamps, scale 1), one recording per device of 50 to 108 samples. Both mouse wheels sent only whole notches (every delta exactly +120 or -120): the coarse wheel 70 to 1800 ms apart, the finely graded one 18 to 136 ms apart with gaps stepping in roughly 8 ms units. Nothing in the values distinguishes the two wheels; only cadence does, so the expected 'fractional notches from a fine wheel' did not occur and a class for them cannot be detected from this hardware. The precision touchpad sent 120ths between 3 and 66, never a multiple of 120, every 17 to 21 ms. After each stroke its values fell to an alternating 4 and 5 with gaps widening to 30, 43 and 134 ms before stopping, which is consistent with the system synthesising inertia in the legacy wheel stream; it is not proof, because lift-off was not marked in the recording. No recording contains horizontal movement or a held modifier, so the sign of sideways deltas and Shift/Ctrl behaviour are still unobserved.

> **Stale** — `watches "crates/liminalkit-shell/tests/scroll_traces/**"` was matched by `94fe8ac3`, which touched `crates/liminalkit-shell/tests/scroll_traces/fine-notched-wheel.trace`. See [REVIEW-REQUIRED.md](REVIEW-REQUIRED.md#what-a-coarse-wheel-a-finely-graded-wheel-and-a-precision-touchpad-send-through-winit-on-windows).

### Headless frame cost from 720p to 4K on one laptop

`verified` · `@pixelkit.evidence.frame-bench-resolution-sweep/1`

Full redraw of one operational screen (panel, 40-row table, 60-row list, six label sizes, AA shapes), warm text cache, 60 frames, on a 13th Gen Intel i7-13700H laptop: 1280x720 p50 1.03 ms / p95 1.14 ms, 7.9 MiB resident; 1920x1080 p50 1.97 / p95 2.27 ms, 12.6 MiB; 1920x1080 at 1.5x p50 2.07 / p95 2.38 ms; 2560x1440 at 1.5x p50 3.23 / p95 3.76 ms, 27.6 MiB; 3840x2160 at 2x p50 9.77 / p95 11.04 ms, 45.2 MiB. Cold first frames 10 to 42 ms. Cost is close to linear in pixel count; 4K is under one 60 Hz frame for a full repaint. liminalkit only: no egui or Freya comparison yet.
